description.narrative: Chad is among the neighboring countries that has received the most displaced Sudanese. As of 31/3/24, Chad had 570,686 refugees <(>&<)> 165,499 returnees in a dozen camps <(>&<)> villages with high-pressing needs. The situation is worrying as WASH standards are notmet. The availability of safe drinking water in all sites is inadequate. Oxfam survey in Mar-24 found that 72% of households in Farchana <(>&<)> Allacha camps have problems accessing water because of distance or insufficient # of water points. Most of the latrines <(>&<)> showers built are overcrowded: there is need of 2,025 latrines <(>&<)> showers. Open defecation is widespread, exacerbated by poor hygiene practices. This heightened the risk of disease outbreaks, especially as the rainy season approaches and as there isno solid waste collection <(>&<)> management system. Influx of refugees and returnees continues to put pressure on food and income.There is strong competition for the few existing opportunities. As a result, incomes have decreased, restricting HH ability to afford basic food items given high prices. Poor HH face food consumption deficits, despite developing negative coping strategies, including meal sharing. They are mainly dependent on food aid. As a result, poor HH are IPC3. In the absence of food aid, they would be inIPC4 Women, girls, and people with specific needs (inc. people with disabilities, chronically ill, people from ethnic minorities) are most at risk of GBV, and forced family separation (CPC Oct-23). According to the protection needs assessmentconducted in the Mitché, Farchana <(>&<)> Allacha camps by the Protection Cluster, there is an urgent need to provide cash for protection and distribution of solar lamps, but also strengthen community protection mechanisms, and facilitating access to services for GBV survivors. Oxfam <(>&<)> SAHKAL propose WASH, FSL and Protection activities in these priority locations to assist 20K people (80% women and children). Gender <(>&<)> protection are mainstreamed in all activities

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Intermon is a member of Oxfam International, a confederation of 17 independent national organisations working in more than 90countries. Oxfam works on six goals that support the shared vision of a just world without poverty: help people claim their right to a better life; champion equal rights for women; saving lives, now and in the future; safeguard global food supplies; help people claim a fairer share of natural resources; and increase money for basic services. For 70 years, Oxfam has been running emergency responses, development projects and campaigning at the grass roots level to tackle poverty.
